title: Devices and RoomOS
blurb: Phones, RoomOS, HELD versus caller ID, media ports, and macros that stay on the device.

lessons.summary: Control Hub claims phones, the Webex App, ATAs, and RoomOS devices into one organization. Emergency location does not use the same method on all of them.
objectives: Name caller ID as the non-HELD path

sections.h: Resync after you enable emergency calling
paragraphs: HELD-capable MPP phones need a resync or reinitialization, or they pick up the configuration on the next check. The article allows that the check can take up to 24 hours.
A phone that has not resynced still looks registered and still has the old emergency behavior.

paragraphs: Room devices are claimed in Control Hub and expose xAPI. Macros run on the device. Cloud commands use the granted xAPI path.
Do not assume a room device is an MPP phone for HELD. Check the emergency article for that model.

lessons.title: What the phone sends
lessons.summary: HELD is RFC 5985. The phone asks RedSky over HTTPS on port 443. The location object is PIDF-LO, RFC 4119.
objectives: Build a wiremap before the test

diagram.caption: Allow the two host names. Map the network.

flow.title: A registration is not a location

steps.label: Learn LLDP or BSSID or IP
steps.detail: Whatever the model reports has to exist in the wiremap.

steps.label: HTTPS to the documented hosts
steps.detail: api.wxc.e911cloud.com and wxc.e911cloud.com, port 443.

steps.label: Return the dispatchable location
steps.detail: Street, floor, and room, as the emergency article describes.

steps.label: Test before you promise 911
steps.detail: 933 is the test pattern in the emergency article.

paragraphs: RFC 5985 is HELD. RFC 4119 is PIDF-LO. Cisco's article is how Webex uses them, not a replacement for the RFCs.
SIP itself remains RFC 3261. Location is an extra object, not a new call-control protocol.
The HELD company ID and secret in Control Hub tie the organization to the RedSky customer. Cisco says it does not store your portal password.
A mismatch warns you. Proceeding overwrites the previous account.

lessons.title: Soft clients, shared lines, and callback
lessons.summary: A cellular Webex App hands 911 to the native dialer. Shared-line emergency routing follows the selected line's location. The callback number has to be answered.
objectives: Route shared-line emergency by the selected line

diagram.caption: The handset, the line, and the callback are three checks.

steps.label: On a cellular client, 911 goes to the native dialer
steps.detail: The emergency article describes that handoff. The Webex location is not what the carrier sees for that call.

steps.label: Select a line
steps.detail: Emergency routing follows the selected line's location, not HELD alone.
steps.inspect: Shared lines article and the emergency article

steps.label: Pick a number that answers
steps.detail: Line number, location default, or another user or virtual line in the same location. An auto attendant that hangs up after hours is a bad callback.

steps.label: Inbound block relaxes after an emergency call
steps.detail: The article describes a 60-minute relaxation of the workspace inbound block after an emergency call.
steps.inspect: Do not invent a longer window

sections.h: What Webex Calling does not store
paragraphs: The emergency article says Webex Calling does not store the emergency service address on the PSTN path. RedSky or the PSTN path you configured is doing that job.
International locations use the PSTN for emergency calling. Enhanced emergency calling in the article is not a claim about every country.

cite.label: Enhanced emergency calling for Webex Calling

paragraphs: The article says an MPP emergency call cannot be hung up locally. Plan for that in training.
933 is still the test, not a live PSAP drill, unless you have arranged one.

fault.symptom: The PSAP calls back and gets a disconnect.

lessons.title: Media ports and ICE
lessons.summary: When ICE succeeds, the app and the devices talk directly on documented UDP ranges. Signaling ports for trunks are a different table.

diagram.caption: Optimized media is a port range, not a wish.

steps.label: ICE succeeds
steps.detail: The port reference says the cloud media relay is removed and the apps send media on 8500-8699. Audio is 8500-8599 and video is 8600-8699.
steps.inspect: Allow it inside the network too

steps.label: ICE succeeds
steps.detail: Devices use 19560-19661 for that direct path.
steps.inspect: VG400 ATA is a wider range in the same table. Do not collapse them

steps.label: Signaling is TCP
steps.detail: Certificate-based trunks need 5062. Registration-based trunks need 8934. Those are not media ports.
steps.inspect: Local gateway listen port is customer-chosen

steps.label: Encrypt the media
steps.detail: RFC 3711 is SRTP. The port reference describes SRTP over UDP toward Webex Calling.
steps.inspect: Do not disable it to make a test pass

paragraphs: Media stays on the cloud relay path the port reference lists, including the broader destination ranges.
A firewall that allows only the direct ranges will pass optimized calls and fail the rest. Allow what the table says for both cases.
Phones may reuse SIP source ports in 5060-5280. The port reference tells you not to pin source ports on the NAT if that stops translation.
The September 07, 2026 note on that article expanded the phone source range from 5060-5080 to 5060-5280.

quiz.q: Certificate trunk signaling to Webex Calling uses

quiz.why: Do not turn it off for a test.

quiz.q: Phone SIP source ports in the 2026 note
quiz.why: NAT must be able to translate overlaps.

lab.title: Two firewall lines
lab.goal: Write the direct media ranges and the trunk signaling ports.
lab.check: You also wrote that non-optimized media uses the broader table.

fault.title: Only the direct range is open
fault.symptom: Calls fail unless both parties are on the LAN.
fault.log: SYNTHETIC: firewall allows 19560-19661 and blocks the cloud media destinations.
fault.fix: Allow the cloud media path from the port reference as well.

lessons.title: RoomOS xAPI and macros
lessons.summary: RoomOS xAPI is the on-device command language. Cloud xAPI posts a command to a granted device. A macro runs locally. Neither one should contain a cloud token.
objectives: Look up commands instead of inventing them
Keep tokens out of the macro

diagram.caption: Catalog on the device. Grant in the cloud. Secret in neither.

flow.title: A macro and a cloud command

steps.label: Search the xAPI reference
steps.detail: Command and status names come from roomos.cisco.com/xapi.
steps.inspect: The device developer guide is the cloud wrapper

steps.label: Run locally
steps.detail: A macro can call xAPI on that device. It does not need your Webex bot token to do that.

steps.label: POST a command if you must
steps.detail: Same organization, device granted, scope from the developer guide.

steps.label: Confirm the device is online
steps.detail: An offline device fails the cloud command. The macro, if loaded, is a separate question.

paragraphs: If a function is not in the xAPI reference, this lab will not pretend a JavaScript helper exists.
Copy examples from the current RoomOS documentation when you write a macro.

sections.h: Emergency calling is not a macro
paragraphs: 933 and HELD are Control Hub and RedSky behavior. A macro that intercepts calls is a good way to break emergency calling.
Do not put 911 logic in a macro unless the emergency article tells you to, which it does not.

fault.title: Token in the macro
fault.symptom: The macro file in email includes a bearer token.

lessons.title: Day-two device checks
lessons.summary: Registration, media, and emergency configuration fail in different ways. The port reference, the devices list, and 933 answer different questions.

steps.label: Check registration
steps.detail: Devices use signaling source ports 5060-5280 toward 8934 in the QoS table. Local gateways use 5062 or 8934 depending on trunk type.

steps.label: Check the UDP ranges
steps.detail: Direct ranges only apply when ICE succeeds. Otherwise use the relay ranges.

steps.label: Test location separately
steps.detail: A call with audio can still have the wrong floor.

steps.label: After emergency changes
steps.detail: Do not wait 24 hours if you can resync.

paragraphs: The port reference recommends turning off SIP ALG. It can break encrypted signaling even though you think it is helping.
Check the firewall vendor's instructions. This lab does not invent CLI.
Non-HELD phones use caller ID for emergency location, per the article's list. They can still register and pass audio.
Eligibility for migration is a later topic. A working phone is not automatically a migratable phone.

quiz.why: Audio can be fine and the floor wrong.
Vendor CLI is theirs, not this lab's.

fault.symptom: TLS signaling fails in ways that look random.

sections.h: Dedicated Instance phones are a different registration
paragraphs: Phones on Dedicated Instance register to that Unified CM, with the voice service domain and DNS forwarder from that track.
Multi-tenant MPP registration uses the Webex Calling port table. Say which phone is which.

Do not mark a model eligible from memory.
